names.official: Income tax on individuals

taxes.base: Employment, pension and business income of individuals.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers and pension funds withhold it.

rate.headline: 9% to 44% (2026 scale)
details: 2026 scale for salaries, pensions and business profits: 9% on the first EUR 10,000, 20% on the next 10,000, 26% on the next 10,000, 34% on the next 10,000, 39% on the next 20,000 and 44% above EUR 60,000; lower scales apply by number of children and for people under 30 (PwC).
The scale of 2024, the year of the revenue, was different.
As summarised by PwC (review of 8 September 2026), not checked against the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

names.official: Taxes on interest and other taxes on individuals, and the tax on pensions (AGAGE)
names.native: Φόρος τόκων και λοιποί φόροι φυσικών προσώπων

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: taxes on interest and other taxes on individuals (EUR 760 million) and a tax on pensions (AGAGE, EUR 627 million).

rate.headline: Set by the Income Tax Code
details: Eurostat records EUR 126 million of income taxes under the social security funds; the list does not say which line.

legalRefs.locator: sheet EL, D51A C02 and C03

names.official: Income tax on corporations

taxes.base: Profit of companies and other legal entities.

rate.headline: 22% standard (credit institutions 29%)
details: The standard corporate income tax rate is 22% for entities other than credit institutions; 29% applies to credit institutions in certain cases (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 8 September 2026), not checked against the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

rate.headline: Set by the tonnage tax regime

legalRefs.locator: sheet EL, D51E C02, D51D C01

names.official: Employers’ social security contributions

taxes.base: Gross pay up to a monthly ceiling (EUR 7,761.94 from 1 January 2026).

rate.headline: 21.79% of gross pay
details: Since 1 January 2025 contributions are 21.79% for the employer and 13.37% for the employee, 35.16% in all (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 8 September 2026), not checked against the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

instruments.explanation: Pension contributions EUR 9.8 billion and other contributions EUR 3.2 billion in 2024.

names.official: Employees’ social security contributions

taxes.base: Gross pay up to the same ceiling.

rate.headline: 13.37% of gross pay
details: See the employers’ line for the sources (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 8 September 2026), not checked against the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

instruments.explanation: The list gives the households’ contributions as one amount, all by employees: pension EUR 10.1 billion, other EUR 4.5 billion.

names.official: Value added tax

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Greece and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 24% standard; 13% reduced
details: 24% for everything not listed as reduced or super-reduced; 13% on ready-to-eat food, non-alcoholic drinks, basic foodstuffs and other goods (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 8 September 2026), not checked against the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).

names.official: Import duties

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on at the pump.

instruments.explanation: The biggest excise: EUR 3.9 billion on domestic and EUR 0.2 billion on imported.
